EarthProsp Atlas

Mineral prospectivity for every land cell on Earth, from AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings (2024) plus gravity, lithosphere, faults, plate boundaries, volcanoes, land cover, terrain and Sentinel-2 alteration. Shown at H3 resolution 4 (~1,770 km² per hexagon), averaged from 4,489,547 resolution-6 cells.

What the colour means

“Any deposit” is the PU-bagged gradient-boosting score, calibrated so its mean over land matches an assumed deposit density. A commodity or mineral system colours by P(deposit) × P(class | deposit). “Model disagreement” is the spread between bagged models. Scales stretch to the 99th percentile of each view.

How well it works

Where not to trust it

“Hide extrapolation” blanks hexagons where most cells fall outside the area of applicability: their features are unlike any training deposit (Meyer & Pebesma 2021), so the score there is a guess. Labels are still densest in the US, and AlphaEarth partly sees mining disturbance itself, so treat bright known districts as expected rather than as discoveries.
